idea:
GitHub issue #45 on mtgibbs/pi-cluster-mcp: Pi-hole stats are primary-only — the secondary is never polled (HA DNS observability gap).

Pi-hole stats are collected from the primary only. PIHOLE_URL is unset, so it defaults to pihole-web, whose Service selector is app: pihole. The secondary runs as app: pihole-secondary and the client has no secondary support, so it is never polled. On our HA DNS (two Pi-hole instances), stats only reflect one of the two resolvers; queries served by the secondary are invisible, and a secondary-only auth/health problem would not show up in get_dns_status. The brainrot CronJob iterates both hosts explicitly (HOSTS="192.168.1.55 192.168.1.56").

Suggested fix: support a list of Pi-hole hosts (env or config), not a single PIHOLE_URL. Authenticate and fetch stats per instance; aggregate totals and/or surface per-instance health so a single-node failure is visible.

# Spec: Pi-hole secondary stats (HA DNS observability)

## 1. Why · [R]

`src/clients/pihole.ts` reads one host from `PIHOLE_URL` (default `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local`,
whose Service selects `app: pihole`). The secondary Pi-hole runs as `app: pihole-secondary`, so the client
never contacts it: `get_dns_status` reports one of two resolvers, queries answered by the secondary are
invisible, and a secondary-only auth or health failure never surfaces. The brainrot CronJob in the cluster
already iterates both hosts explicitly (`HOSTS="192.168.1.55 192.168.1.56"`); the MCP client should do the same.

## 2. Outcomes · [R]

1. The client resolves a **list** of Pi-hole base URLs from `PIHOLE_HOSTS` (comma-separated). When
   `PIHOLE_HOSTS` is unset or blank, the list is exactly `[http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local]` —
   today's single-primary behaviour, unchanged.
2. Every instance is contacted at its **own** base URL: each gets its own `POST <base>/api/auth` and its
   own authenticated `GET <base>/api/stats/summary`. A session id obtained from one host is never sent to
   another, and a host is never fetched without a session obtained from that same host.
3. `getSummaryAcrossInstances()` returns per-instance results plus an aggregate: `dns_queries_today`,
   `ads_blocked_today`, `unique_domains`, `queries_forwarded` and `queries_cached` are the **sum** across
   healthy instances; `ads_percentage_today` is recomputed as `blocked / total * 100` (rounded to one
   decimal); `domains_being_blocked` (the gravity list size, identical on both nodes) and `unique_clients`
   (the same LAN clients are visible from either node) are the **max**, never the sum;
   `gravity_last_updated` is taken from the **most recent** `gravity.last_update`.
4. A failing instance does not hide the others: it is reported with `ok: false` and a `reason`; the
   aggregate covers only the healthy instances; and the result carries a `summary` string with a verdict
   (`all N instances healthy` / `degraded — N/M responding`). If **every** instance fails there is nothing to
   aggregate, so the run throws and `get_dns_status` reports `statsError` — the pre-existing behaviour for a
   fully unreachable Pi-hole.
5. `get_dns_status` output gains `piholeInstances` (per-instance `{ url, ok, queriesToday, blockedToday,
   reason? }`), `instancesTotal`, `instancesResponding`, and a `stats.summary` verdict line. Its existing
   keys (`stats.queriesToday`, `stats.blockedToday`, `statsError`, …) keep working.

## 3. Entities · [E]

| Name | Kind | Exact definition |
|---|---|---|
| `PIHOLE_HOSTS` | env var | Comma-separated Pi-hole **base URLs**, e.g. `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local,http://pihole-secondary-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local`. Empty/unset ⇒ single primary. Trailing `/` trimmed. |
| `getPiholeUrls(): string[]` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | Parsed `PIHOLE_HOSTS`; falls back to `[PIHOLE_URL]`. |
| `PiholeInstanceStats` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | `{ url: string; ok: boolean; summary?: PiholeStats; reason?: string }` — `reason` present **iff** `ok === false`; `summary` present **iff** `ok === true`. |
| `PiholeAggregate` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | `{ instancesTotal: number; instancesResponding: number; allHealthy: boolean; summary: PiholeStats; summaryVerdict: string }` |
| `PiholeRunResult` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | `{ instances: PiholeInstanceStats[]; aggregate: PiholeAggregate }` |
| `getSummaryAcrossInstances(): Promise<PiholeRunResult>` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | The only multi-instance-aware read. It never throws when **some** instances fail — each failure is reported as `ok: false` with a `reason`. If **every** instance fails it throws (no healthy instance exists to build `aggregate.summary` from), and `get_dns_status` turns that into `statsError`, as it does today. |
| `summaryVerdict` | string field | `"all N instances healthy"` (all ok, N ≥ 1) · `"degraded — R of N Pi-hole instances responding"` (0 < R < N). Not produced when R = 0: the run throws instead. |
| `resetPiholeAuthState(): void` | new export, `src/clients/pihole.ts` | Clears the per-host session cache, in-flight logins and rate-limit cooldown. For tests only; production code must not call it. |

`get_dns_status` response additions: `piholeInstances`, `instancesTotal`, `instancesResponding`,
`stats.summary`. No new tools, no tool renames, no input-schema changes.

## 4. Approach · [A]

Turn the client's module-level singletons into **per-host state** keyed by base URL: one session cache, one
in-flight login and one rate-limit cooldown per host (`Map<url, …>`), so the #48 single-flight guarantee and
the #44/#48 error wording survive unchanged, and the 429 cooldown of one host cannot suppress logins to the
other. `piholeFetch(endpoint)` fans out over `getPiholeUrls()` internally for the tools that already work
per-call (`getSummary`, `getTopItems`, `getQueryTypes`, `getStatus`, `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`,
`getRecentQueries`), and `updateGravity()` POSTs to every host — a gravity update is a per-instance operation,
so HA should not diverge. `getSummaryAcrossInstances()` is the only multi-instance-aware read: it fetches each
host's `stats/summary`, converts with the existing `convertStatsToLegacy`, and aggregates as in §2.3.
`src/tools/dns.ts` calls it and keeps `stats.*` populated from the aggregate so existing consumers see the
same shape plus the per-instance list.

Rejected: (a) a second `PIHOLE_SECONDARY_URL` env var — hard-codes the topology at two and duplicates every
code path; (b) a new `get_pihole_instances` tool — touches tool registration, `tools.test.ts` registry
expectations and the read-only scope matrix for no extra observability; (c) round-robin or "primary unless it
fails" selection — silently hides a down node, which is the bug being fixed.

## 5. Scope · [S]

**In scope**
- `src/clients/pihole.ts` — per-host state, `PIHOLE_HOSTS`, `getPiholeUrls`, `getSummaryAcrossInstances`,
  aggregate types, `resetPiholeAuthState`.
- `src/tools/dns.ts` — `get_dns_status` renders per-instance results + aggregate.
- `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary-stats.test.ts` (new) — the six client tests in §11.
- `src/__tests__/dns-instances.test.ts` (new) — the `get_dns_status` handler test in §11.

**Out of scope**
- `k8s/` manifests, `package.json`, CI, auth/scopes, tool registry, other tools/clients, README/CLAUDE.md.
- `test_dns_query` / `diagnose_dns` pod selection (`app=pihole`) — exec-based, unchanged.
- Per-instance top-domains or query logs (`get_pihole_queries`, `get_pihole_whitelist` keep their existing
  fan-out semantics but gain no aggregate).

## 6. Prior facts · [S]

- `src/clients/pihole.ts:4-5` — `PIHOLE_URL` / `PIHOLE_PASSWORD` are read into module-level consts at import
  time; `pihole-auth.test.ts:42-46` therefore re-imports the module with `vi.resetModules()` after stubbing env.
- `src/clients/pihole.ts:8-13,124-163` — one `sessionId`, one `authInFlight`, one `rateLimitedUntil`;
  `authenticate()` single-flights logins (issue #48) and `login()` throws diagnosable errors (issue #44).
  Error text is load-bearing: `pihole-auth.test.ts:95-97,142-144,162-163` asserts on it.
- `src/clients/pihole.ts:231-252` — `piholeFetch` prefixes `${PIHOLE_URL}/api/`, adds the `sid` header.
- `src/clients/pihole.ts:255-321` — `PiholeStats` legacy shape and `convertStatsToLegacy`; `getSummary()`
  must keep its signature and `Promise<PiholeStats>` return because `pihole-auth.test.ts` calls it directly.
- `src/tools/dns.ts:68-101` — stats are fetched only when `includeStats && piholePods.some(ready)`, wrapped in
  one try/catch that sets `result.statsError`; `result.stats` keys are as listed in §2.5.
- `src/__tests__/write-tool-gates.test.ts:38-45` mocks `../clients/pihole.js` with `updateGravity`,
  `getFullStats`, `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`, `getRecentQueries`; `dns.ts` must not import any other client
  export at module scope or that mock returns `undefined` for it (the new call is made inside the handler, and
  the dns test supplies its own mock).
- CLAUDE.md: summary-first output for list tools (`src/utils/summary.ts`) — "If a tool states a conclusion,
  it must be correct"; array-form commands, no new dependencies; deployment whitelist and RBAC untouched here.

## 7. Norms · [N]

- Keep the existing error-message conventions: auth failures name `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN`, 429s say the word
  "rate-limit"/"suppressed" and never blame the credential. Per-host messages must include the base URL.
- No new dependencies; no new env vars beyond `PIHOLE_HOSTS`; no `any` (ESLint `no-explicit-any` is an error).
- Tests: vitest, `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` + `vi.stubEnv` + `vi.resetModules()` fresh-import, as in
  `pihole-auth.test.ts`. Per-instance assertions use exact counts (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`), never "at most".
- Comments explain *why* (the repo comments cite issue numbers); keep them short.

## 8. Safeguards · [S]

- **No secrets in output.** `reason` carries only status text / error message — never the password, never a
  session id. The `sid` header must never appear in tool output.
- **No fail-open.** A host whose login fails or whose fetch throws is `ok: false` with a reason; it must never
  be dropped silently or counted as healthy. `allHealthy` is true only when every configured instance is ok.
- **No cross-host auth.** A session id must never be sent to a host it was not obtained from.
- **No new auth suppression across hosts**: host A's 429 cooldown must not prevent a first login to host B.
- **No write-tool widening.** `update_pihole_gravity` stays single-call, rate-gated, `readOnly: false`; it must
  not fan out per call in a way that bypasses `GRAVITY_COOLDOWN_MS`.
- **No API break:** `getFullStats`, `getStatus`, `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`, `getRecentQueries`,
  `getTopItems`, `getQueryTypes`, `updateGravity` keep their exported names, signatures and return types.
- No changes to `k8s/`, CI, auth, or tool registration.

## 9. Tasks · [O]

- T1: Add `PIHOLE_HOSTS` parsing (`getPiholeUrls`), per-host session/in-flight/cooldown state, and
  `resetPiholeAuthState` to `src/clients/pihole.ts`, keeping `pihole-auth.test.ts` green.
- T2: Add `PiholeInstanceStats`, `PiholeAggregate`, `PiholeRunResult` and `getSummaryAcrossInstances()`
  (sum/max/most-recent aggregation + `summaryVerdict`) to `src/clients/pihole.ts`.
- T3: Render per-instance stats in `get_dns_status` in `src/tools/dns.ts` (`piholeInstances`,
  `instancesTotal`, `instancesResponding`, `stats.summary`), keeping `statsError` behaviour for total failure.
- T4: Add `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary-stats.test.ts` with the six tests and exact fixtures in §11 (rows 1-5b).
- T5: Add `src/__tests__/dns-instances.test.ts` with the two `get_dns_status` handler tests and fixtures in §11.

## 10. Acceptance criteria (EARS) · [O]

- **AC1** When `PIHOLE_HOSTS` is set to two URLs and a summary is requested, the system shall issue one
  `POST /api/auth` and one `GET /api/stats/summary` per URL, each addressed at that URL's base.
- **AC2** If a Pi-hole host is configured, then the system shall send only a session id obtained from that
  same host on requests to it (host B must not receive host A's sid, nor an absent sid).
- **AC3** When summaries from two instances with different numbers are aggregated, the system shall report
  `dns_queries_today = 1400`, `ads_blocked_today = 280`, `ads_percentage_today = 20`,
  `domains_being_blocked = 1000` (max), `unique_domains = 70` (sum), `clients_ever_seen = 30` (sum),
  `unique_clients = 10` (max — the same LAN clients are visible from either node),
  `queries_forwarded = 1050`, `queries_cached = 250`.
- **AC4** When two instances report different `gravity.last_update` values, the aggregate's
  `gravity_last_updated.relative` shall be derived from the larger timestamp (fixture: `days === 2`).
- **AC5** When one instance is down or its login is rejected, the system shall return that instance with
  `ok: false` and a non-empty `reason`, keep the other instance's numbers as the whole aggregate, set
  `instancesResponding` to 1 of 2, set `allHealthy` to false, and set `summaryVerdict` to
  `degraded — 1 of 2 Pi-hole instances responding`.
- **AC6** If every configured instance fails, then the system shall throw rather than return an aggregate
  built from zero healthy instances, and `get_dns_status` shall report that failure in `statsError` (its
  pre-existing behaviour) instead of returning zeroed totals or a healthy verdict.
- **AC7** If `PIHOLE_HOSTS` is unset or empty, then the system shall contact exactly
  `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local` and `summaryVerdict` shall read `all 1 instances healthy`.
- **AC8** When `get_dns_status` runs against two responding instances, the system shall return
  `piholeInstances` of length 2 with `queriesToday` 1000 and 400, `instancesTotal: 2`,
  `instancesResponding: 2`, and `stats.summary === "all 2 instances healthy"`.
- **AC9** When `get_dns_status` runs with one responding and one unreachable instance, the system shall
  return `instancesResponding: 1`, a `piholeInstances` entry whose `reason` contains `503` for the down host,
  `stats.queriesToday === 400`, and shall not set `statsError`.
- **AC10** If `get_dns_status` is called with `includeStats: false`, then the system shall not call
  `getSummaryAcrossInstances`.

## 11. Verification

`verify.sh` checks (each prints one PASS/FAIL; any FAIL ⇒ non-zero exit):

1. **`getPiholeUrls` exported** — grep `src/clients/pihole.ts` for `export function getPiholeUrls` and for the
   literal `PIHOLE_HOSTS`. *Fails before the change:* neither string exists today. Proves the env var exists.
2. **`getSummaryAcrossInstances` exported** — grep for `export async function getSummaryAcrossInstances`.
   *Fails today:* the function does not exist.
3. **New client test file exists** — `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary-stats.test.ts` must exist.
   *Fails today:* the file is absent.
4. **Client tests present, with pinned fixtures** — greps that file for the six exact `it(...)` titles below
   and for the expected literals beside them. *Fails today:* no file. Literals are what stop a wrong
   implementation shipping with matching wrong tests.
5. **Client tests pass** — `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-secondary-stats.test.ts`.
   *Fails on a wrong implementation:* aggregation, per-host auth, or degradation logic misbehaving.
6. **Handler test file exists + titles** — `src/__tests__/dns-instances.test.ts` and its two `it(...)` titles.
   *Fails today:* absent. Asserts the tool-level shape (`'1000'`/`'400'` fixture pins, `'"all 2 instances healthy"'`,
   `'instancesResponding'` `toBe(1)`) so a client-only change that never reaches `get_dns_status` cannot pass.
7. **Handler tests pass** — `npx vitest run src/__tests__/dns-instances.test.ts`.
8. **Existing auth regression tests still pass** — `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts`.
   *Fails if:* per-host refactoring broke single-flight, the 429 cooldown, or the error wording.

## 12. Open questions

- Exact in-cluster URLs for `PIHOLE_HOSTS` (the secondary Service name — `pihole-secondary-web`?) are set by
  the operator in `k8s/deployment.yaml`; this spec deliberately does not touch manifests, and the default
  keeps single-primary behaviour when the var is absent.
- Whether `get_pihole_queries` / `get_pihole_whitelist` should merge across instances or stay primary-only is
  left for a follow-up; today's fan-out semantics are preserved.
- Per-instance `topQueries` / `topBlocked` remain the primary's (they come from `getFullStats`); merging
  top-domain lists across instances is out of scope.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gate for spec: pihole-secondary-stats (GitHub issue #45).
#
# Runs from the repo root after lint/typecheck/test/build have passed. Asserts only on artefacts this
# change creates: the PIHOLE_HOSTS env var and its exports, the two new test files, the exact test
# titles AND the fixture/expected literals in them (so a wrong implementation cannot ship with
# matching wrong tests), and targeted runs of the new tests plus the existing #44/#48 auth regressions.
#
# Must FAIL on the pre-implementation tree: the env var, both exports and both new test files do not
# exist yet, so checks 1-4 and 6-8 fail there.

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

CLIENT=src/clients/pihole.ts
TOOL=src/tools/dns.ts
CLI_TEST=src/__tests__/pihole-secondary-stats.test.ts
DNS_TEST=src/__tests__/dns-instances.test.ts
AUTH_TEST=src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts

FAILURES=0
VITEST_TIMEOUT=240

pass() { printf 'PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1)); }

# grep -q against a possibly-missing file: absent content counts as "not found", never a crash.
has() { # has <regex> <file>
  [ -f "$2" ] && grep -qE -- "$1" "$2"
}

# has_all <regex> <file> <literal...> : file must contain the regex AND every literal (fixed string).
has_all() {
  local regex="$1" file="$2"; shift 2
  has "$regex" "$file" || return 1
  local needle
  for needle in "$@"; do
    grep -qF -- "$needle" "$file" || return 1
  done
  return 0
}

run_vitest() { # run_vitest <label> <file>
  local label="$1" file="$2"
  if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
    fail "$label (missing $file)"
    return
  fi
  if timeout "$VITEST_TIMEOUT" npx vitest run "$file" > "/tmp/pih-sec-stats-${label}.log" 2>&1; then
    pass "$label"
  else
    fail "$label (see /tmp/pih-sec-stats-${label}.log)"
    tail -n 30 "/tmp/pih-sec-stats-${label}.log"
  fi
}

echo "== pihole-secondary-stats gate =="

# --- 1. PIHOLE_HOSTS multi-host configuration exists in the client -------------------------------
if has 'export[[:space:]]+(async[[:space:]]+)?function[[:space:]]+getPiholeUrls' "$CLIENT" \
  && grep -qF -- 'PIHOLE_HOSTS' "$CLIENT"; then
  pass "1. client exports getPiholeUrls and reads PIHOLE_HOSTS"
else
  fail "1. client exports getPiholeUrls and reads PIHOLE_HOSTS"
fi

# --- 2. The multi-instance read is exported ------------------------------------------------------
if has 'export[[:space:]]+async[[:space:]]+function[[:space:]]+getSummaryAcrossInstances' "$CLIENT"; then
  pass "2. client exports getSummaryAcrossInstances"
else
  fail "2. client exports getSummaryAcrossInstances"
fi

# --- 3. New client test file exists -------------------------------------------------------------
if [ -f "$CLI_TEST" ]; then
  pass "3. $CLI_TEST exists"
else
  fail "3. $CLI_TEST exists"
fi

# --- 4. Client tests: exact titles AND their pinned fixtures -------------------------------------
# 4a. every instance is contacted at its own URL, with its own session id
if has_all "polls every configured Pi-hole host with its own login" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'http://primary.test/api/auth' 'http://secondary.test/api/auth' \
  '/api/stats/summary' 'sid-primary' 'sid-secondary' 'toHaveBeenCalledTimes(4)'; then
  pass "4a. multi-host polling test pins both auth URLs, both sids and 4 fetch calls"
else
  fail "4a. multi-host polling test pins both auth URLs, both sids and 4 fetch calls"
fi

# 4b. aggregation: distinct per-host fixtures + the exact expected aggregate (a "first one wins"
#     implementation cannot produce 1400 / 280 / 20 / 1050 from 1000+400 and 200+80).
if has_all "aggregates totals across instances instead of reporting one resolver" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'dns_queries_today' 'toBe(1400' 'ads_blocked_today' 'toBe(280' \
  'ads_percentage_today' 'toBe(20' 'domains_being_blocked' 'toBe(1000' \
  'unique_domains' 'toBe(70)' 'clients_ever_seen' 'toBe(30' \
  'unique_clients' 'toBe(10)' 'queries_forwarded' 'toBe(1050' \
  'queries_cached' 'toBe(250' 'all 2 instances healthy'; then
  pass "4b. aggregation test expects summed totals (1400/280/20%), summed uniques (70/30), maxed gravity/clients (1000/10)"
else
  fail "4b. aggregation test expects summed totals (1400/280/20%), summed uniques (70/30), maxed gravity/clients (1000/10)"
fi

# 4c. gravity: instances disagree, newest must win (primary is 4 days old in the fixture)
if has_all "uses the most recent gravity update when instances disagree" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'gravity_last_updated' 'toBe(2'; then
  pass "4c. gravity test expects the newest last_update (days === 2, not the 4-day primary)"
else
  fail "4c. gravity test expects the newest last_update (days === 2, not the 4-day primary)"
fi

# 4d. degradation: the failing node is visible, the verdict says degraded, no secrets leak
if has_all "surfaces a down or mis-authenticated secondary instead of silently dropping it" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'ok).toBe(false' '/401/' 'toBe(1)' 'toBe(false' \
  'toBe(1000)' 'toBe(200)' \
  'degraded — 1 of 2 Pi-hole instances responding'; then
  pass "4d. degradation test expects ok:false + 401 reason, 1 of 2 responding, degraded verdict"
else
  fail "4d. degradation test expects ok:false + 401 reason, 1 of 2 responding, degraded verdict"
fi

# 4e. backwards compatibility: unset PIHOLE_HOSTS keeps today's single-primary target
if has_all "keeps single-primary behaviour when PIHOLE_HOSTS is unset" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local' 'getPiholeUrls' 'toBe(1)' 'all 1 instances healthy'; then
  pass "4e. single-primary test pins the default URL, instancesTotal 1 and its verdict"
else
  fail "4e. single-primary test pins the default URL, instancesTotal 1 and its verdict"
fi

# 4f. total failure must NOT fail open with zeroed totals: the run throws and the tool reports statsError
if has_all "throws when no configured instance responds, rather than reporting zeroed totals" "$CLI_TEST" \
  'rejects.toThrow' 'none of the 2 configured instances responded'; then
  pass "4f. all-instances-down test expects a rejection, not zeroed totals"
else
  fail "4f. all-instances-down test expects a rejection, not zeroed totals"
fi

# --- 5. Client tests actually pass --------------------------------------------------------------
run_vitest "5. client multi-instance tests" "$CLI_TEST"

# --- 6. Tool-level tests: file, titles and pinned expectations ----------------------------------
if [ -f "$DNS_TEST" ]; then
  pass "6a. $DNS_TEST exists"
else
  fail "6a. $DNS_TEST exists"
fi

# 6b. healthy two-instance get_dns_status output (handler-level, not just a client grep)
if has_all "get_dns_status reports both Pi-hole instances and their combined totals" "$DNS_TEST" \
  'piholeInstances' 'instancesTotal' 'toBe(2)' 'instancesResponding' \
  'all 2 instances healthy' 'toBe(1400)' 'summary' 'toBeUndefined'; then
  pass "6b. get_dns_status test expects 2 instances, 1400 combined queries and the healthy verdict"
else
  fail "6b. get_dns_status test expects 2 instances, 1400 combined queries and the healthy verdict"
fi

# 6c. single-node failure must be visible in the tool output, without statsError
if has_all "get_dns_status marks a single-node failure visible instead of hiding it" "$DNS_TEST" \
  'instancesResponding' 'toBe(1)' '503' 'toBe(400)' \
  'degraded — 1 of 2 Pi-hole instances responding'; then
  pass "6c. get_dns_status degradation test expects 1 of 2 responding, 503 reason, 400 queries"
else
  fail "6c. get_dns_status degradation test expects 1 of 2 responding, 503 reason, 400 queries"
fi

# 6d. the handler must actually route through the multi-instance read
if has 'getSummaryAcrossInstances' "$TOOL" && has 'getSummaryAcrossInstances' "$DNS_TEST"; then
  pass "6d. get_dns_status calls getSummaryAcrossInstances (tool and its test both reference it)"
else
  fail "6d. get_dns_status calls getSummaryAcrossInstances (tool and its test both reference it)"
fi

# --- 7. Tool tests actually pass ----------------------------------------------------------------
run_vitest "7. get_dns_status instance tests" "$DNS_TEST"

# --- 8. Existing #44/#48 auth regressions still hold after the per-host refactor ----------------
run_vitest "8. existing pihole auth regression tests" "$AUTH_TEST"

echo
if [ "$FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "ALL CHECKS PASSED"
  exit 0
fi
echo "$FAILURES CHECK(S) FAILED"
exit 1
